examples.en: The police called in the suspect yesterday and questioned him.
The suspect said from the start that he had done nothing wrong.

examples.ko: 뉴스에서 피의자 얼굴은 보여 주지 않았어요.
examples.en: The news did not show the suspect's face.

examples.ko: 변호사가 피의자와 두 시간 동안 이야기했어요.
examples.en: The lawyer talked with the suspect for two hours.
The suspect in the case was caught last night.
The suspect's family cried in front of the reporters.

explain: 피의자는 경찰이나 검찰이 조사하는 단계의 사람이고, 재판에 넘겨지면 '피고인'이라고 불러요. 뉴스에서는 자주 들리지만 일상 대화에서는 거의 쓰지 않아요.
explain_en: 피의자 is the person under investigation by police or prosecutors; once the case goes to trial the person is called 피고인. You hear it often in the news but almost never in everyday talk.

examples.ko: 우리 삼촌은 해병으로 군 생활을 했어요.
examples.en: My uncle served in the military as a marine.
The marine unit is near the coast.

examples.ko: 해병이 되려면 체력 시험을 통과해야 해요.
examples.en: To become a marine, you have to pass a fitness test.

examples.ko: 형이 해병에 지원해서 다음 달에 입대해요.
examples.en: My older brother applied to the marines and enlists next month.
The marines are training on the sand.
The marine in the movie looked really cool.

explain: 해병은 해군과 따로 있는 부대 사람이고, 바다에서 땅으로 올라가 싸우는 일을 맡아요. 군대 이야기에서는 '육군', '해군', '공군'과 함께 '해병대'라고도 자주 말해요.
explain_en: 해병 is a member of the marine corps, which is separate from the navy and fights by landing from the sea. In talk about the military, people often say 해병대 (the Marine Corps) next to 육군, 해군, and 공군.

examples.en: I saw a knight's armor from long ago at the museum.
Armor is heavy, so it is hard to wear for long.

examples.ko: 영화 주인공이 은색 갑옷을 입고 나왔어요.
examples.en: The hero of the movie appeared in silver armor.
The armor got dented when the sword hit it.

examples.ko: 아이가 종이로 갑옷 모양 옷을 만들었어요.
examples.en: The child made an armor-shaped outfit out of paper.
It is dangerous to fight without armor.

explain: 갑옷은 '입다'와 함께 쓰고, 몸 전체를 감싸는 옛날 쇠 옷을 떠올리면 돼요. 가슴만 막는 '방탄조끼'와는 달라요. 요즘은 역사, 게임, 영화 이야기에서 주로 들어요.
explain_en: 갑옷 goes with the verb 입다 and brings to mind the old metal suit that covers the whole body. It differs from a 방탄조끼 (bulletproof vest), which protects only the chest. Today you mostly hear it in talk about history, games, and movies.

examples.en: A big donor gave a scholarship fund to the school.

examples.ko: 그 회사는 고액 연봉으로 사람을 뽑아요.
examples.en: That company hires people with a very high salary.

examples.ko: 현금으로 고액을 내는 사람은 많지 않아요.
examples.en: Not many people pay a large sum in cash.
More students are getting expensive private tutoring.
The hospital bill is a large sum, so I am worried.
It is a contest with a big prize.

explain: 고액은 '고액 연봉', '고액 기부'처럼 다른 말 앞에 붙여 쓸 때가 많아요. 반대말은 '소액'이고, 일상 대화에서는 그냥 '큰돈'이라고도 해요.
explain_en: 고액 is often placed before another noun, as in 고액 연봉 or 고액 기부. Its opposite is 소액, and in everyday talk people also just say 큰돈.

examples.en: I submitted my work to a poster contest.
The contest prize is bigger than I thought.
My friend won first place in the contest.

examples.ko: 이번 공모전은 다음 주까지 신청해야 해요.
examples.en: You have to apply for this contest by next week.

examples.ko: 공모전을 준비하느라 요즘 잠을 못 자요.
examples.en: I can't sleep these days because I'm preparing for a contest.
Many contests are held for college students.

explain: 공모전은 사진, 영상, 글, 아이디어를 내서 겨루는 대회를 말할 때 써요. '공모'는 공개적으로 작품을 모은다는 뜻이라서, 누구나 낼 수 있고 심사로 뽑는 대회에 잘 어울려요. 외래어 '콘테스트'와 비슷하지만 공모전은 작품을 모집해서 심사한다는 느낌이 더 분명해요. '공모전에 나가다', '공모전에 내다'처럼 말해요.
explain_en: 공모전 is the word for a competition where people submit photos, videos, writing, or ideas. 공모 means openly collecting entries, so the word suits contests that anyone can enter and that are judged. It is close to the loanword 콘테스트, but 공모전 more clearly implies collecting and judging submissions. Typical phrases are 공모전에 나가다 and 공모전에 내다.

en: side with; go along with; follow

examples.en: I did not go along with my friend's opinion.

examples.ko: 다들 그 말에 동조해서 회의가 빨리 끝났어요.
examples.en: Everyone sided with that remark, so the meeting ended quickly.
He sided with the majority's claim.

examples.ko: 아무도 그의 생각에 동조할 사람이 없어요.
examples.en: There is nobody who would side with his idea.
More people are going along with the mood.
Please don't pretend to go along with me on purpose.

explain: '동조하다'는 '의견에 동조하다'처럼 '~에' 붙여 써요. '동의하다'는 내 생각도 같다는 뜻이고, 동조하다는 다른 사람이나 분위기를 따라가는 느낌이 있어요. 말보다 글이나 뉴스에서 더 자주 나와요.
explain_en: 동조하다 takes ~에, as in 의견에 동조하다. 동의하다 means your own view is the same, while 동조하다 carries a feeling of following another person or the mood. It shows up more in writing and the news than in speech.

examples.en: We have a mock interview at school tomorrow.
I did worst in English on the mock exam.
We held a practice drill at the fire station.
I held a mock trial with my classmates.
Try practicing stocks with simulated investing.
It's only a simulated situation, so you don't need to be nervous.

explain: 모의는 단독으로는 거의 안 쓰고 '모의 면접', '모의시험', '모의 훈련'처럼 다른 명사 앞에 붙어요. 수능을 준비하는 학생들은 '모의고사'를 자주 봐요. 실제와 똑같이 해 본다는 느낌이 있어요.
explain_en: 모의 is almost never used alone; it attaches before another noun, as in 모의 면접, 모의시험, and 모의 훈련. Students preparing for the college entrance exam often take a 모의고사 (practice test). It carries the feeling of doing something exactly as if it were real.

examples.en: The team is struggling because of the boss's incompetence.
If your incompetence shows, you lose people's trust.
He admitted his own incompetence.
Citizens are angry at the government's incompetence.
Incompetence can be fixed by learning.
Incompetence and laziness are different from each other.

explain: 무능은 능력이 없다는 점을 가리키는 명사예요. 반대말은 '유능'이에요. 꽤 강한 비판이라서 사람 앞에서 직접 말하는 일은 드물고, 글이나 뉴스에서 더 자주 나와요.
explain_en: 무능 is the noun for lacking ability, and its opposite is 유능. It is a fairly harsh criticism, so people rarely say it to someone's face; it appears more in writing and the news.

examples.en: That boss was incompetent and ruined the company.
I'm hopeless at cooking.
It is hard to work under an incompetent leader.
Sometimes I feel that I am incompetent.
There was criticism that the government was incompetent.

examples.ko: 무능하게 보일까 봐 질문을 못 했어요.
examples.en: I couldn't ask a question for fear of looking incompetent.

explain: 무능하다의 반대말은 '유능하다'예요. 사람에게 쓰면 강한 비난이라서 부드럽게 말할 때는 '서툴다'나 '못하다'를 써요. '요리에는 무능해요'처럼 자기 자신에게 농담으로 쓰기도 해요.
explain_en: The opposite of 무능하다 is 유능하다. Said about another person it is a strong accusation, so to soften it people use 서툴다 or 못하다. People also use it jokingly about themselves, as in 요리에는 무능해요.

examples.en: A seal sticker was attached to the box.
If you break the seal, you can't get a refund.

examples.ko: 전설 속 괴물은 천 년 동안 봉인에서 풀리지 못했어요.
examples.en: In the legend, the monster stayed in its seal for a thousand years.
The exam papers arrived at the school still sealed.
The seal on the storage case was broken.

examples.ko: 이 영화는 봉인의 힘이 풀리면서 시작해요.
examples.en: This movie starts when the power of the seal is released.

explain: 봉인은 뜯으면 티가 나게 붙이는 도장이나 스티커처럼 현실 물건에도 쓰고, 판타지에서는 힘이나 괴물을 가두는 마법에도 많이 나와요. '봉인을 풀다', '봉인이 풀리다'처럼 말해요. '밀봉'은 공기가 안 통하게 막는 느낌이 더 강해요.
explain_en: 봉인 is used for real things like a stamp or sticker that shows if something was opened, and in fantasy it often means a magic seal that locks up a power or monster. You say 봉인을 풀다 or 봉인이 풀리다. 밀봉 leans more toward closing something airtight.

examples.en: The staff member sealed the evidence box.
Put the secret document in the safe and seal it.
The wizard seals the monster inside a book.

examples.ko: 택배를 보내기 전에 입구를 봉인할 거예요.
examples.en: I will seal the opening before sending the package.
I wanted to lock away an old memory.
They show how to seal it in a video.

explain: '봉인하다'는 뜯으면 알 수 있게 닫거나, 판타지에서 힘을 가둘 때 써요. '밀봉하다'는 공기가 안 들어가게 꼭 막는 것이라 음식 포장에 더 잘 맞아요. 기억이나 감정을 억누를 때도 비유로 써요.
explain_en: 봉인하다 means to close something so that opening it would show, or to lock away a power in fantasy. 밀봉하다 means shutting it tight so no air gets in, which suits food packaging better. It is also used figuratively for suppressing memories or feelings.

examples.ko: 배우가 분장을 하는 데 세 시간이 걸려요.
examples.en: It takes the actor three hours to get into makeup.

examples.ko: 핼러윈 날 아이들이 무서운 분장으로 모였어요.
examples.en: On Halloween the kids gathered in scary costumes and makeup.

examples.ko: 분장 덕분에 완전히 다른 사람처럼 보였어요.
examples.en: Thanks to the makeup, he looked like a completely different person.
The makeup was all wiped off by sweat.
Please take photos of the play's makeup.

examples.ko: 분장 담당자가 머리와 얼굴을 손봐 줬어요.
examples.en: The makeup staff fixed up my hair and face.

explain: 분장은 연극, 영화, 행사에서 역할에 맞게 얼굴과 모습을 꾸미는 일이에요. 평소에 하는 '화장'과 달리 다른 인물이나 모습으로 바꾼다는 점이 달라요. '분장을 하다', '분장을 지우다'처럼 써요.
explain_en: 분장 is dressing and making up the face to fit a role in a play, movie, or event. Unlike everyday 화장, the goal is to change into another character or look. You say 분장을 하다 and 분장을 지우다.

examples.en: The child dressed up as a tiger.
I will dress up as a pirate for Halloween.
The actors act while made up as old people.
I don't know how I should do my costume makeup.
I read the script while getting made up.

examples.ko: 친구들이 서로 분장해 주고 사진을 찍었어요.
examples.en: My friends did each other's makeup and took photos.

explain: '유령으로 분장하다'처럼 '~(으)로 분장하다' 형태로 써요. '꾸미다'는 더 넓게 예쁘게 하는 일이고, 분장하다는 다른 인물이나 모습처럼 보이게 하는 일이에요. '변장하다'는 남이 못 알아보게 바꾸는 것이라 달라요.
explain_en: It is used in the pattern ~(으)로 분장하다, as in 유령으로 분장하다. 꾸미다 is broader and just means making something look nice, while 분장하다 means making yourself look like another character. 변장하다 is different: it means changing your look so that others can't recognize you.

en: assume; suppose; introduce (a bill) for discussion

examples.ko: 이 계획은 비가 오는 경우를 상정해서 만들었어요.
examples.en: This plan was made assuming it would rain.
I prepared by supposing the worst case.
The chair put a new item on the meeting's agenda.

examples.ko: 모든 학생이 영어를 잘한다고 상정하면 안 돼요.
examples.en: You must not assume that every student is good at English.
The customer we have in mind is a worker in their twenties.
Please think through two possible cases.

explain: '상정하다'는 쓰임이 두 가지예요. 글에서는 '비 오는 경우를 상정하다'처럼 '가정하다'와 비슷하게 쓰는데 더 딱딱해요. 회의나 국회에서는 '안건을 상정하다'처럼 토론 자리에 올릴 때 써요.
explain_en: 상정하다 has two uses. In writing, as in 비 오는 경우를 상정하다, it is close to 가정하다 but stiffer. In meetings or the National Assembly, as in 안건을 상정하다, it is used for putting an item up for discussion.

examples.en: The police search and seizure began in the morning.
Confiscated items are kept in a warehouse.
Items that were seized are hard to get back.

examples.ko: 시험 중 휴대전화 압수는 학교 규칙이에요.
examples.en: Confiscating phones during exams is a school rule.
The shop owner was flustered by the sudden seizure.
Seizures of illegal copies are increasing.

explain: 압수는 경찰이나 학교처럼 권한이 있는 쪽이 물건을 가져가는 일이에요. 뉴스에서는 '압수 수색'이라고 한 덩어리로 자주 나와요. 훔치는 것과 달리 법이나 규칙에 따라 가져간다는 점이 달라요.
explain_en: 압수 is used when someone with authority, such as the police or a school, takes an item away. In the news it often appears as the set phrase 압수 수색. Unlike stealing, it is done under a law or rule.

examples.en: The teacher confiscated the game console during class.
Customs confiscated the fruit in the bag.

examples.ko: 규칙을 어기면 물건을 압수할 수 있어요.
examples.en: If you break the rules, your things can be confiscated.
The police seized the computer and investigated.
They give back confiscated items later.

examples.ko: 부모님이 제 휴대폰을 압수해서 연락을 못 했어요.
examples.en: My parents took my phone away, so I couldn't get in touch.

explain: '압수하다'는 가져가는 사람이 경찰, 세관, 선생님처럼 권한이 있는 사람이에요. 친구끼리 장난으로 뺏을 때는 '뺏다'를 써요. 뺏기는 쪽은 '압수당하다'라고 말해요.
explain_en: The one doing 압수하다 is someone with authority, such as the police, customs, or a teacher. When friends take something playfully, they use 뺏다. The person it is taken from says 압수당하다.

examples.en: An international expo was held in Yeosu.
The subway is crowded during the expo.
I looked at new books at a book expo.
I bought expo tickets in advance.
The theme of this expo is the environment.

examples.ko: 엑스포를 보러 외국인 관광객이 많이 와요.
examples.en: Many foreign tourists come to see the expo.

explain: 엑스포는 큰 국제 행사나 산업 전시 이름에 주로 붙고, 작은 행사에는 '박람회'나 '전시회'를 많이 써요. '대전 엑스포', '푸드 엑스포'처럼 이름 뒤에 붙는 경우도 흔해요.
explain_en: 엑스포 mostly appears in the names of large international events or industry shows, while smaller events are usually called 박람회 or 전시회. It is also common as a name tag, as in 대전 엑스포 or 푸드 엑스포.

examples.ko: 우리 지역구 국회의원은 다음 주에 시장을 방문해요.
examples.en: Our district's lawmaker will visit the market next week.

examples.ko: 그 의원은 지역구 주민을 자주 만나요.
examples.en: That lawmaker often meets residents of the district.
The district changed, so the polling place is different.
He won in his district three times in a row.

examples.ko: 저는 지역구 후보와 비례대표 후보에게 각각 투표했어요.
examples.en: I voted separately for a district candidate and a proportional candidate.

examples.ko: 지역구의 오랜 숙원 사업이 드디어 시작됐어요.
examples.en: The district's long-awaited project has finally started.

explain: 지역구는 '비례대표'와 짝으로 자주 나와요. 지역구는 우리 동네 사람을 뽑고, 비례대표는 정당을 보고 뽑아요. 뉴스에서 '지역구 의원'처럼 써요.
explain_en: 지역구 often appears as a pair with 비례대표. With 지역구 you elect a person for your own area, while with 비례대표 you vote by party. In the news you see phrases like 지역구 의원.

examples.en: I saw a huge pyramid in Egypt.
I'm still curious how the pyramids were built.
I want to climb to the top of the pyramid.

examples.ko: 아이들이 컵을 쌓아 피라미드 모양을 만들었어요.
examples.en: The kids stacked cups into a pyramid shape.

examples.ko: 이 회사는 피라미드 구조라서 위에 있는 사람이 적어요.
examples.en: This company has a pyramid structure, so few people are at the top.
Many tourists take photos at the pyramids.

explain: 피라미드는 이집트 유적 말고도 '인구 피라미드', '피라미드 구조'처럼 아래가 넓고 위가 좁은 모양을 빗대어 써요. 또 불법 다단계 사업을 줄여서 '피라미드'라고 말하기도 해요.
explain_en: Besides the Egyptian monuments, 피라미드 is used figuratively for anything wide at the bottom and narrow at the top, as in 인구 피라미드 and 피라미드 구조. People also shorten an illegal multi-level scheme to just 피라미드.

examples.en: The owner shut the dog in the yard.
They built an embankment to hold in the water.
You must not lock a child in a room.
The wizard locks the dragon in a tower.
Don't bottle up your feelings; try talking.
Where is the place where the criminal was locked up?

explain: '가두다'는 '~에 가두다'로 쓰고, 갇히는 쪽은 '갇히다'라고 해요. 사람, 동물, 물, 감정까지 쓸 수 있어요. '넣다'는 그냥 안에 두는 것이고, 가두다는 못 나오게 하는 거예요.
explain_en: 가두다 is used as ~에 가두다, and the one who ends up locked in is expressed with 갇히다. It works for people, animals, water, and even feelings. 넣다 just puts something inside, while 가두다 means making it unable to get out.

examples.en: The test detected bacteria.
The machine detects even small bits of metal.

examples.ko: 연구팀이 물에서 중금속을 검출한 사실을 알렸어요.
examples.en: The research team announced that they detected heavy metals in the water.

examples.ko: 이 장치로 연기를 검출할 수 있어요.
examples.en: You can detect smoke with this device.
It is hard to detect a weak signal.

examples.ko: 오염 물질을 검출하면 바로 연락 주세요.
examples.en: If you detect a pollutant, please contact us right away.

explain: '검출하다'는 검사나 기계로 숨어 있는 물질이나 신호를 찾아낼 때 쓰고, 과학과 뉴스에서 자주 나와요. 그냥 물건을 찾을 때는 '찾다'를 써요. '발견하다'는 우연히 알게 될 때도 쓰지만 검출하다는 도구를 쓴 결과예요.
explain_en: 검출하다 is used when a test or machine finds a hidden substance or signal, and it appears often in science and the news. For simply looking for an object, use 찾다. 발견하다 can also be an accidental discovery, but 검출하다 is a result obtained with a tool.

examples.en: He did not give in to the pressure.
The enemy army finally surrendered.

examples.ko: 아이의 울음에 굴복해서 장난감을 사 줬어요.
examples.en: I gave in to my child's crying and bought the toy.
If you yield to temptation, dieting is hard.
I don't want to submit to fate.

examples.ko: 그 나라는 협박에 굴복할 생각이 없어요.
examples.en: That country has no intention of yielding to threats.

explain: '굴복하다'는 '압력', '유혹', '협박'처럼 강한 힘 뒤에 '에'를 붙여 써요. '항복하다'는 싸움이나 경기에서 졌다고 손드는 일이고, 굴복하다는 힘에 눌려 뜻을 꺾는 느낌이에요. 가벼운 일에는 '지다'를 써요.
explain_en: 굴복하다 takes 에 after a strong force such as 압력, 유혹, or 협박. 항복하다 is raising your hands because you lost a fight or game, while 굴복하다 feels like giving up your will under force. For minor things, use 지다.

examples.en: This bug lives as a parasite on animals' bodies.
Mistletoe is a plant that lives off trees.
Organisms that live as parasites need a host.
I don't want to live off my parents.
A small tick lived as a parasite on the dog.
An attitude of trying to live off others is not good.

explain: '기생하다'는 '~에 기생하다'로 쓰고, 다른 생물에서 영양을 얻어 사는 생물에게 써요. 사람에게 쓰면 남에게 기대어 사는 부정적인 느낌이에요. 비슷한 '얹혀살다'는 남의 집에 같이 사는 쪽에 더 가까워요.
explain_en: 기생하다 is used as ~에 기생하다 for living things that get their nourishment from another organism. Said about people it has a negative feel of living off someone. The similar 얹혀살다 is closer to living in someone else's home.

examples.en: The scientists named the new species 'Rainbow'.

examples.ko: 새로 발견된 병을 명명하는 데 시간이 걸렸어요.
examples.en: It took time to name the newly discovered disease.
They will name the new road 'Cheongchun-ro'.
The company decided to name the new product 'Haeoreum'.

examples.ko: 이 꽃을 처음 명명한 사람이 누구예요?
examples.en: Who was the first person to name this flower?

examples.ko: 새로 찾은 동굴을 어떻게 명명할지 투표했어요.
examples.en: We voted on what to name the newly found cave.

explain: '~을 ~(으)로/라고 명명하다' 형태로 써요. 새로 발견한 것, 제품, 길 이름 같은 공식적인 자리에서 쓰고, 평소에는 '이름을 짓다', '이름을 붙이다'라고 말해요. 아기 이름도 '명명하다'보다 '이름을 짓다'가 자연스러워요.
explain_en: It is used in the pattern ~을 ~(으)로/라고 명명하다. It fits formal situations such as new discoveries, products, and road names; in ordinary talk people say 이름을 짓다 or 이름을 붙이다. Even for a baby's name, 이름을 짓다 sounds more natural.

examples.en: The magician pulled a rabbit out of a hat.
My dream as a child was to be a magician.

examples.ko: 마술사의 손놀림을 눈으로 따라갈 수 없었어요.
examples.en: I couldn't follow the magician's hands with my eyes.
We invited a magician to the birthday party.
That magician is good at card tricks.
I clapped for the street magician.

explain: 마술사는 손재주와 기술로 신기한 장면을 보여 주고, 판타지의 '마법사'는 진짜 마법을 써요. 그래서 마술은 무대에서 보고 마법은 이야기 속에서 만나요.
explain_en: A 마술사 shows amazing tricks with skill and sleight of hand, while a fantasy 마법사 uses real magic. So you see 마술 on stage and meet 마법 in stories.

examples.en: This bowl has a flower pattern.
They put a traditional pattern on the hanbok.

examples.ko: 벽지 문양은 눈에 띄지 않는 걸로 골랐어요.
examples.en: I picked a wallpaper pattern that doesn't stand out.
The geometric design on the carpet is pretty.

examples.ko: 건물 벽에 새겨진 문양의 뜻이 궁금해요.
examples.en: I'm curious about the meaning of the design carved on the building wall.
The price changes depending on the fabric pattern.

explain: 문양은 옷, 그릇, 건물에 반복해서 들어가는 장식 모양이에요. '무늬'는 일상에서 더 흔하게 쓰고, 문양은 전통, 문화, 디자인 이야기에서 더 자주 써요. 옷의 줄무늬는 '줄 문양'보다 '줄무늬'가 자연스러워요.
explain_en: 문양 is the decorative shape repeated on clothes, dishes, or buildings. 무늬 is more common in daily talk, while 문양 appears more in talk about tradition, culture, and design. For stripes on clothes, 줄무늬 is more natural than 줄 문양.

examples.en: The news says the rebels have taken control of the city.
A ceasefire was reached between the government army and the rebels.
The rebel leader gave a speech.

examples.ko: 영화 속 반군은 숲속에 숨어 지냈어요.
examples.en: In the movie, the rebels lived hidden in the forest.

examples.ko: 반군에게 무기를 대 주는 나라가 있어요.
examples.en: There is a country that supplies weapons to the rebels.

examples.ko: 반군의 공격으로 마을 사람들이 피난을 갔어요.
examples.en: The villagers fled because of the rebels' attack.

explain: 반군은 '정부군'과 짝으로 뉴스에 자주 나와요. 비슷한 '반란군'은 질서를 어지럽힌다는 비난의 느낌이 더 강하고, 반군은 상황을 설명하는 말투에 가까워요. 일상 대화에서는 거의 쓰지 않아요.
explain_en: 반군 often appears in the news as a pair with 정부군. The similar 반란군 carries a stronger tone of blame for disturbing order, while 반군 sounds more like neutral reporting. It is rarely used in everyday talk.

examples.en: This movie is really big in scale.
I was amazed by the scale of the concert hall.
The budget was short, so we cut back the scale of the event.
That person is generous and thinks on another scale.
Stories about space are different in scale from the start.
It's a small shop, but the scale of the ideas is big.

explain: 스케일은 영어 scale에서 온 말이지만 한국어에서는 '규모가 크다', '통이 크다'는 칭찬으로 자주 써요. '스케일이 크다'가 가장 흔하고, 작다고 말할 때는 '규모가 작다'를 더 많이 써요.
explain_en: 스케일 comes from English 'scale', but in Korean it is often used as praise meaning big in size or generous in spirit. 스케일이 크다 is the most common pattern; to say something is small, people more often say 규모가 작다.

examples.en: Many migratory birds come to this wetland.

examples.ko: 습지는 물이 잘 빠지지 않는 땅이에요.
examples.en: A wetland is land where water does not drain easily.
People who protect wetlands gathered.
I looked at the reeds at the Suncheon Bay wetland.
The path led into a wetland, so my shoes got wet.
It was a class to observe the plants and insects of the wetland.

explain: 습지는 환경과 자연 보호 이야기에서 쓰는 말이고, '늪'은 더 깊고 빠질 것 같은 곳을 말해요. '갯벌'은 바다 가까이에서 밀물과 썰물 때 드러나는 땅이라 달라요.
explain_en: 습지 is the word used in talk about the environment and nature protection, while 늪 is a deeper place where you might sink. 갯벌 is different: it is the land near the sea that is exposed at low tide.
